input.goal: Rinse the chickpeas, then place the chickpeas on a towel and lightly towel dry them so they aren't wet from rinsing. You can remove any loose skins at this time too.

sub_goals.text: Drain the chickpeas and rinse the can.
Rinse and drain the chickpeas in the colander.
Transfer the chickpeas to paper towels and dry them.
Remove loose skins from the chickpeas.
Transfer the chickpeas to a baking tray and continue removing loose skins.

events.description: The person opens the can of chickpeas using a pull tab or can opener.
events.relevance: Provides access to the chickpeas inside the can.

events.description: A popping or cracking sound is heard as the can seal is broken.
events.relevance: Indicates the can has been successfully opened.

events.description: The person tips the can to pour the aquafaba liquid down the sink drain.
events.relevance: Removes the initial canning liquid from the chickpeas.

events.description: The person runs tap water into the can to rinse the remaining liquid.
events.relevance: Cleans the residual starchy liquid from the can and chickpeas.

events.description: The sound of running water splashing into the metal can.
events.relevance: Confirms the rinsing action is occurring.

events.description: The person pours the chickpeas from the can into a colander.
events.relevance: Transfers the chickpeas to a tool suitable for thorough rinsing.

events.description: The person runs water over the chickpeas in the colander.
The person shakes the colander up and down to drain the excess water.
events.relevance: Removes the bulk of the rinsing water before towel drying.

events.description: The person dumps the rinsed chickpeas from the colander onto paper towels.
events.relevance: Moves the chickpeas to an absorbent surface for drying.

events.description: The person gently rubs or pats the chickpeas with another paper towel.
events.relevance: Dries the chickpeas so they are not wet for the next cooking step.

events.description: The person pinches individual chickpeas to slide off their translucent skins.
events.relevance: Improves the texture of the chickpeas by removing the loose skins.

events.description: The person discards the removed skins into a pile or a waste bin.
events.relevance: Separates the unwanted skins from the prepped chickpeas.

events.description: The person moves the dried chickpeas from the paper towels onto a baking tray.
events.relevance: Prepares the chickpeas for roasting or further processing.

events.description: The person picks off any remaining loose skins from the chickpeas now on the tray.
events.relevance: Ensures all loose skins are removed before cooking.

decision_points.why: Deciding to drain the liquid directly from the can before fully emptying the chickpeas is a distinct procedural choice.
Moving from rinsing inside the can to using a colander for a more thorough rinse requires fetching a new tool and changing the action.
Transitioning from washing to drying requires setting up paper towels and changing the physical interaction with the chickpeas.
Moving from bulk drying to the meticulous, individual task of peeling skins is a major shift in action and focus.
Deciding to transfer the chickpeas to a baking tray to finish the peeling process involves a spatial relocation and preparing for the next recipe stage.
The task is complete; deciding to stop peeling skins and move on to the next recipe step (like seasoning or roasting) is a real decision.
